arguments.topic: automated brain extraction skull stripping MRI deep learning

rows.title: Automated neonatal nnU-Net brain MRI extractor trained on a large multi-institutional dataset.
rows.dataset: HEAL study (433 training participants); NIH and dHCP evaluation datasets
rows.summary: ANUBEX enables automatic neonatal brain extraction across high- and low-resolution MRI, achieving significantly higher aggregate Dice scores than five comparator methods.

rows.title: Brain extraction on MRI scans in presence of diffuse glioma: Multi-institutional performance evaluation of deep learning methods and robust modality-agnostic training.
rows.method: Deep learning brain extraction with modality-agnostic training
rows.modality: Multiparametric brain MRI with brain tumors
rows.dataset: Private institutional cohorts and TCIA collections (3,340 scans)
rows.summary: Evaluates deep learning architectures and introduces modality-agnostic training for multi-institutional brain extraction in tumor-affected MRI without retraining for available modalities.

rows.title: Towards fully automated deep-learning-based brain tumor segmentation: is brain extraction still necessary?
rows.method: Deep learning tumor segmentation pipeline trained and tested without skull stripping
rows.metric_values: Brain extraction method choice can compromise tumor segmentation performance by up to 15.7% (metric not specified)
rows.summary: Shows that brain extraction choices can impair tumor segmentation and that training on non-skull-stripped images provides competitive performance with reduced processing time.

rows.title: A general skull stripping of multiparametric brain MRIs using 3D convolutional neural network.
rows.method: EnNet: ensemble neural network based on 3D convolutional neural networks
rows.dataset: UPMC private cohort and TCIA (815 cases with or without GBM)
rows.summary: Introduces an automatic multicenter skull-stripping method for healthy and pre-/post-operative GBM scans, comparing 15 modality combinations and finding the best performance with all modalities.

rows.title: An End-To-End Pipeline for Fully Automatic Morphological Quantification of Mouse Brain Structures From MRI Imagery.
rows.method: DeepBrainIPP: deep learning skull stripping with data augmentation, atlas registration, and dedicated direct segmentation of small structures
rows.modality: In vivo and ex vivo mouse brain T2-weighted MRI
rows.dataset: Private cohort (172 images augmented to 4,040 samples)
rows.metric_values: Skull stripping: mean Dice 0.96, residual volume 2.18%; atlas registration: mean cross-correlation 0.98; small-structure segmentation: mean Dice 0.89, residual volume error 5.32%
rows.summary: Provides an automated, web-accessible mouse brain processing pipeline combining skull stripping and atlas registration with direct segmentation for small brain structures.

rows.title: k-strip: A novel segmentation algorithm in k-space for the application of skull stripping
rows.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
rows.method: k-strip: deep learning skull stripping directly in complex-valued k-space
rows.dataset: not stated (four institutional datasets totaling approximately 200,000 MRI slices)
rows.metric_values: Dice 92%–99%; Hausdorff distance <5.5 pixels; Dice up to 99% for slices above the eye region
rows.summary: Demonstrates skull stripping directly in MRI k-space while preserving phase information and enabling anonymization before image reconstruction.

rows.title: Automated pediatric brain tumor imaging assessment tool from CBTN: Enhancing suprasellar region inclusion and managing limited data with deep learning.
rows.method: Separate nnU-Net models for skull stripping, whole-tumor segmentation, and enhancing-tumor segmentation
rows.modality: Pediatric brain multiparametric MRI using T2, FLAIR, and T1-Gd sequences
rows.dataset: Private multi-institutional cohort (527 patients; 336 for skull stripping and 489 for tumor segmentation)
rows.metric_values: Skull stripping: Dice 0.98 ± 0.01 (median 0.98) for single- and multi-parametric models; single-/multi-parametric Dice correlation r > 0.80, P < .05; whole tumor: T2 Dice 0.84 ± 0.17 (median 0.90), FLAIR Dice 0.82 ± 0.19 (median 0.89); enhancing tumor: T1-Gd+FLAIR Dice 0.65 ± 0.35 (median 0.79), T1-Gd+T2 Dice 0.64 ± 0.36 (median 0.79)
rows.summary: Develops pediatric skull-stripping models that include sellar/suprasellar regions and tumor segmentation models that accommodate missing MRI sequences in limited-data settings.

rows.title: RU-Net: skull stripping in rat brain MR images after ischemic stroke with rat U-Net.
rows.method: RU-Net: U-shaped deep network with residual connections, batch normalization, and pooling-index transmission
rows.modality: Rat brain diffusion-weighted imaging and T2-weighted MRI after ischemic stroke
rows.dataset: Private cohorts (two in-house datasets, each containing 55 subjects)
rows.summary: Introduces an end-to-end skull-stripping network for rat brain MRI after ischemic stroke that outperforms several existing methods on DWI and T2WI datasets.

rows.title: SynthStrip: skull-stripping for any brain image.
rows.method: SynthStrip: learning-based brain extraction trained on synthetic images generated from anatomical segmentations
rows.modality: Brain MRI across varied contrasts, acquisition protocols, and resolutions
rows.dataset: not stated (synthetic training dataset and unnamed evaluation datasets spanning newborns to adults)
rows.summary: Uses highly varied synthetic training data to enable a single brain-extraction model to generalize across imaging protocols and populations without target-contrast training data.

rows.title: ASMCNN: An efficient brain extraction using active shape model and convolutional neural networks
rows.method: ASMCNN: modified active shape model and CNN with CRF, Gaussian-process, and rule-based contour refinement
rows.modality: Brain MRI processed as 2D sagittal image sequences
rows.summary: Combines group-specific shape priors with CNN-based contour refinement to improve skull stripping across variations in brain morphology and image intensity.
